deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Gauss's 'Geometria situs' notes on self-intersecting closed plane curves ('Tracte'). A curve with n double points ('Knoten') is recorded as a 'Gauss word': the sequence of crossing labels met along one traversal, each label occurring twice. The previous page treats n = 4. There Gauss gives 105 = 8!/(2^4·4!) words in canonical (first-occurrence) order. He states the parity criterion: number the places 0..2n−1, and in a realisable closed curve each pair of places belonging to one crossing must contain one even and one odd number. He shows the 24 = 4! parity words for n = 4 are all possible. He then remarks that for n ≥ 5 the criterion is no longer sufficient, citing abcadcedbe and abcabdecde as impossible.

This page is the promised complete lexicographic list for n = 5. It contains exactly the 120 = 5! words on aabbccddee that satisfy the parity condition, i.e. the bijections from the even places {0,2,4,6,8} to the odd places {1,3,5,7,9}. (The total number of canonical words is 10!/(2^5·5!) = 945.)

Layout: each block begins with a full 10-letter word. The following lines give only the tail; the prefix is understood from the block head. The blocks are:
- 1–6: aabb + 6 letters
- 7–12: aabc + 6
- 13–24: aabcd + 5
- 25–30: abba + 6
- 31–36: abbc + 6
- 37–48: abbcd + 5
- 49–54: abcab + 5
- 55–66: abcad + 5
- 67–72: abccb + 5
- 73–84: abccd + 5
- 85–96: abcdb + 5
- 97–108: abcdd + 5
- 109–120: abcde + 5

The block sizes are 6,6,12,6,6,12,6,12,6,12,12,12,12, summing to 120. Each size is forced by the parity constraint. For example, after the prefix abcad the free places 5–9 must take b on an even place, c and d on odd places, and e on one even and one odd place: 2·3! = 12.

Gauss stars seven words as impossible despite satisfying parity:
- 53 abcabdecde
- 57 abcadcedbe
- 64 abcadebdec
- 91 abcdbceade
- 93 abcdbedaec
- 112 abcdeadebc
- 115 abcdecdabe

(My check, in modern terms.) Join two crossings by an edge of the 'interlacement graph' when their occurrences alternate in the word.
- For 57 this graph is the 5-cycle a–b–e–d–c–a.
- For 53, 64 and 91 it is two triangles sharing one vertex (a 'bowtie').
- In both cases every degree is even, so parity holds. But some non-interlaced pair has exactly one common interlaced neighbour, an odd number, so Gauss's/Dehn's second condition fails and the word is non-planar.

Rotations of the cyclic word map starred words to starred words: 57 rotated by one place, after relabelling, is 93; 53 rotated is 64. So the stars mark whole cyclic classes of non-realisable words.
errors: No arithmetic or logical errors found. Block sizes and the lexicographic order are consistent with the parity constraint.

I verified four of the seven starred words (53, 57, 64, 91) are non-realisable, and 93 via rotation from 57. I did not exhaustively verify that no unstarred word is non-realisable (e.g. 112, 115 and the rest).

results.what: Enumeration of all 120 Gauss words with 5 crossings satisfying the even/odd (interlacing parity) condition, in lexicographic canonical form
results.modern_name: Gauss words / Gauss code; Gauss's parity condition for planar realisability of closed curves
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass, Werke VIII 'Zur Geometria situs', ed. Stäckel 1900)

results.what: Identification (by stars) of the 7 parity-satisfying 5-crossing words that are not realisable by a plane closed curve, showing the parity condition is insufficient for n>=5
results.modern_name: Insufficiency of Gauss's condition; Gauss code realisability problem (later solved by Nagy 1927, Dehn 1936, Rosenstiehl 1976, Read–Rosenstiehl)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss for the observation (Werke VIII); full characterisation to Dehn / Rosenstiehl

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's parity condition and his observation that it fails for 5 crossings (with the counterexample abcadcedbe) are already published in Werke VIII and well known. This full 120-word table with the starred impossible cases is a notable supporting detail, but not new attribution.

Number of 5-letter Gauss words satisfying the even/odd place condition (bijections evens->odds), matching the 120 entries

Counts for 4 crossings quoted on the previous page

checkable.asserts: In word 57 the non-interlaced pair a,d has exactly one common interlaced letter (odd), so the word is non-realisable despite parity
